title: Song & a Scene
description:
Song & a Scene is a showcase celebrating emerging musical theatre writers and performers.

We’re all familiar with scratch nights for plays and concerts for musicals, but on 18 November at The Union, we’re bringing the two together in a unique showcase that celebrates both song and storytelling.

Our audience will have the chance to see song and book woven together as we present a tapestry of talented creatives and exciting new musical theatre writing.

Presenting:

  • Grace O’Keefe and Thomas F. Arnold with ‘Sense and Sensibility’
  • Neil Bastian with ‘The Mayfly Man’
  • Greg Link, Ewen Christie and Dee Taylor-Thompson with ‘Smile for the Camera’
  • Ben Sheldrick and Chris Burgess with ‘Seven – A Sinful New Musical’
  • Caspar Simonsen with ‘Café! The Musical’
  • Nic Rowley and Jeremy Browne with ‘The Horse’s Mouth’
  • Dylan Zwickel and Step Pażernov with ‘The City of Ember’
  • Louis Eddie-Edwards with ‘Aberfan: A Musical Tragedy’

Produced by Mint Face Productions
address: Union Theatre, 229 Union St, London, SE1 0LR

title: Non Finito: Art in Evolution
description:
“ART in EVOLUTION

A new Live Arts Festival

All the pieces you will see and their creators are on a journey. As will YOU be!

ART ON A JOURNEY TO THE KINGDOM OF WHAT WE ARE AND YET NEVER BECOME!

Non Finito is an artistic patchwork composed of various new performance pieces in a state of evolution, including live music, dance and Theatre. From bare to full production, or from full to bare. Albums that haven’t been recorded yet, played live. An ancient legend illustrated through dance and movement. The tale of a young adventurer, lost on the way to the kingdom, and more.

Dance, theatre, music, color and light!

LINE UP:

  1. DESCENDANTS OF ANANSI by Kofi Mingo

19th 20th and 21st NOV

8 PM

Solo dance piece with space, sound, and a Stick for good measure!

Anansi is trapped in the  digital space. All knowledge and wisdom he once protected has been corrupted by Chaos and it’s minions. His body never to be made whole again.

In order to gain the upper hand in the struggle for freedom, Anansi enlisted the help of an unwilling and unknowing descendant back in the real world. Sound-heavy dance adventure about humanity, evolution, and connection, played by Kofi Mingo.

  1. LUX written & performed by Olivier Sublet
    19th 20th and 21st NOV
    8:30 PM
    “Laurence tells us the story of a young dreamer who departs from his home despite his family’s better judgement, embarking on a journey to the kingdom to obtain a special item that will lead him to success. But along the way he trips and falls through a crack in the earth only to wake up in a barren wasteland, riddled with dangers. He discovers an “Evil” side of himself, and gets to know his shadow. The three entities set off to find their path to the kingdom once again.”

  1. BRNSRGHT
    SAT 21 NOV
    7:30PM – Live unreleased music by prolific composer and artist BRNSRGHT. BRNSRGHT (pronounced “burns right”) is a London-based, Lithuanian-born artist, music producer, and multi-instrumentalist who creates genre-fluid alternative music spanning alternative, rock, and textured soundscapes. He was part of Ivan Michael Blackstock’s Olivier Award-winning show TRAPLORD and has composed music for fashion shows, including London Fashion Week, and works closely with visual artists and choreographers.

  1. STAMATIS SERAPHIM LIVE
    FRI 20 NOV
    7:30PM
    Live unreleased music by long-time EVOL Creation collaborator and friend: Stam!
    Stamatis is a Greek-South African composer, performer, multi-instrumentalist and MD. Their music ranges from film and theatre soundtracks to R&B/Soul and jazz. Stam is the composer and musical director for “LEVEL UP!”, an original musical written by Lucy Watson and directed by Patrick Wilson. Recent credits include GREEN, directed by Meg Schadler and Benedict Esdale; and SEAL BOY, directed by Sean Turner. SEAL BOY marks the second collaboration between Sean and Stamatis, their first being A Midsummer Night’s Dream (starring Kerry Ellis, Jonathan Hyde, Dan Burton and Milly Zero). In-between, they’re writing and producing an R&B/Soul album with Rae Morgan for their band, Rae & the Seraphim, as well as working on their own music.

  1. CONSENSUS LIVE
    THURS 19 NOV
    7:30PM
    Live hip hop set by rapper and scientist CONSENSUS.
    South London rapper Consensus is back with his new album Original ConScience—a blend of hip-hop, grime, and jungle that explores the “Origins of the Universe” through sharp lyricism and standout showmanship. He has led discussions and performed at the highest level, including Johns Hopkins and Cambridge University, earning acclaim from BBC Radio 1Xtra, BBC Radio 6, BBC World News, and the Financial Times. A genre-blurring artist, Consensus transforms particle physics into high-energy rap. Internationally recognised for his CERN-backed project ConCERNed, he has toured across Europe, North America, and Africa, performing at iconic venues and opening for international hip-hop legends.

We are also running stunts and movement workshops

  1. “Original Conscience” Workshop with Consensus
    Thurs 19 NOV
    4PM – 6PM at The Union Theatre
    Fun, creative session on ways to write and perform technical themes and topics.

Learn how to take ideas as complex as astronomy, particle physics and the origins of the universe, and express them as poetry and rap Email olivier@evolcreation.co.uk for more information

  1. “U-N-1-VERSE” freestyle movement workshop with Kofi Mingo
    Fri 20 NOV
    4PM – 6PM at The Union Theatre
    A fusion of Kofi’s all-ages freestyle “movement” programme named “U-N-1 VERSE”. Learn techniques based on simple self-identification, self-awareness, and movement awareness, set to music.
    Click HERE for a Discounted ticket

  2. Screen Combat workshop with Adrian Falconer
    Sat 21 NOV
    9:30AM – 11:30AM at Carpenters and Dockland Centre
    Learn screen combat from actor and stunt coordinator Adrian Falconer (Little Simz, RAYE, The Gentlemen)
    Click HERE for a Discounted ticket

This event is produced by EVOL Creation and TAKA Strike Club, with support from Global Mosaic Foundation.

address: Union Theatre, 229 Union St, London, SE1 0LR

title: Killing It!
description:
In comedy, “to kill” is the highest compliment.

Lola Martin has been killing it every night. And on the last night of her standup tour, she hopes to kill again.

From the mic stand, Lola takes us on her journey through the highs and lows of comedy: courses in “how to be funny”, bombing in front of audiences, a bizarre string of relationships and her rise to comedy fame.

Killing It is a comedy about comedy – and how far someone is prepared to get the laugh. Even if they’re also a suspect in a murder case…

So, just where does she get her material from?

Guest Stars

24th – Reb Day

25th – Phoebe Taylor

26th – Leah Davis
address: Union Theatre, 229 Union St, London, SE1 0LR

title: Throbbin’ Hood & His Messy Men
description:
Wax your bowstrings and spit polish your arrows this Christmas, as Robin is in town to leave you throbbing with excitement!

Things are looking dreary in Frottingham. With the recent absence of King Dicky, his undesirable brother, Prince Andy, takes charge and has put the sadistic Sheriff to task to wring every last penny out of the poor peasants of the town.

It’s down to our virile outlaw hero, Robin, to save the townsfolk from poverty, along with his band of rather outlandish ‘brothers’. And, as the legend foretells, they like to take from the rich and give to the greedy… sorry, needy… twice nightly.

But can Robin ever save Maid Marion from the sweaty grasps of Prince Andy? Can Freya Tucked lead herself from temptation, even when she’s touching the papal cloth? Will we ever find out what happened that fateful night in the forest between Robin and Little John Thomas? Who knows?

Only one thing’s for certain. With all the gang in tow, and the help of a certain Spirit of the Forest to ‘Turn Back Time’, you are in for a filthily funny, shamefully salacious, marvellously messy time at the Union Theatre this Christmas!

What are you waiting for? Get your tickets now!
address: Union Theatre, 229 Union St, London, SE1 0LR

It’s down to our virile outlaw hero, Robin, to save the townsfolk from poverty, along with his band of rather outlandish ‘brothers’. And, as the legend foretells, they like to take from the rich and give to the greedy… sorry, needy… twice nightly.

title: Love Is Never Wasted
description:
A work-in-progress presentation of Rosamund Gravelle’s new play Love Is Never Wasted.

Love Is Never Wasted is set in a stiflingly isolated & mysterious industrialised facility characterised by the maintenance of heavy-duty pipes & spigots.

Jar has decided to stay on after their shift chatting to Doll who has just started theirs, and thankfully the shift has seen only the one Runner, so far. As they chat, Doll slowly opens up to Jar about a loss, but stops wanting to carry out their duties, forcing Jar to choose to stay to make sure Doll doesn’t explode the pipes & lose all the water left in the world, or leave and trust Doll to do the right thing.  Will Doll let pipes explode and lose all the water? Can Jar take a step out of their comfort zone? Or has Doll chosen to be a Runner and leave their world behind, or will they stay with Jar and friendship and what they have always done? And will the mysterious Runner really destroy everything or possibly save them all?

Love Is Never Wasted – a highly commended play by the National Theatre’s script panel – is a disconcerting absurdly comic play, full of heart, provoking questions about what we accept & why – a Gen Z “Waiting for Godot” for the end of the capitalist age.
address: Union Theatre, 229 Union St, London, SE1 0LR

title: A Tree to Save a Forest
description:
When young but hardened climate activists hear about the destruction of a local woodland they are torn. Do they continue protesting oil depots, petrol stations, airports: at the heart of the industries that are wrecking the planet, or do they go local, fighting for this forest and its woodland nursery?

Based on true events, A Tree to Save a Forest is a tense, heart-felt play that asks how far we would go to save what we love. For activist Frankie, the woodland is a distraction from her previous plan to occupy the main runway at Stansted airport. Yasmin grew up going to the nursery, so joins this local fight. Longing for justice, with fast-paced action, humour and monologues rich in self- reflection, the characters are learning who they are and what they are willing to do.

The play follows the characters through the spectacle of protest and through police investigations into them. Yasmin learns her activism requires escaping her comfort zone and risking arrest. Nate finds a sense of belonging in nature that she felt missing from the London queer community where she found herself. Frankie turns from the dramatic, headline-grabbing protest to respecting and protecting what Yasmin is doing.
address: Union Theatre, 229 Union St, London, SE1 0LR

title: These Are Words That Go Together Well
description:
Set in a post-apocalyptic near future, four preteen girls pass the time by performing their very own play to remember their life before. Or at least what they remember of their life before… Luckily they’ve got heaps of DVDs, CDs and books to fill in the blanks!
These Are Words That Go Together Well blends absurdist comedy with gritty drama to celebrate true feminine connection – warts and all!
address: Union Theatre, 229 Union St, London, SE1 0LR
